correctness.rationale: For R=D⋉(Q/D), the nilradical N=0⋉(Q/D) is divided because Q/D is divisible, R/N=D is a valuation domain, and a nonzero nonunit d makes (d,0) a zero-divisor outside N. The canonical-kernel inclusion K⊆N is published, while torsion of Q/D gives N⊆K. The flat resolution 0→D→Q→Q/D→0 has Q⊗_D(Q/D)=0 and (Q/D)⊗_D(Q/D)=0, so Tor_1^D(Q/D,Q/D)≅Q/D and higher D-Tor vanishes. Zhang--Qi Theorem 6.3 then yields Tor_{2m}^R(N,N)=0 and Tor_{2m+1}^R(N,N)≅N; long exact Tor sequences for 0→N→R→D→0 give the mixed and D-D table. Boundary n=0 and n=1 cases were checked separately.

value.rationale: The recent trichotomy is driven by canonical-kernel self-Tor but leaves the odd modules abstract. The fraction-quotient idealization D⋉(Q/D) is a classical, structurally natural test object, and here the recurrence closes to a complete periodic module profile.
